summary: Added mutual exclusivity guard at the top of resolveProjectPath() in mcp-server/src/utils/path-validator.ts. When both project_path and cwd_path are provided the function now throws new Error(MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG) before any other logic runs. The existing mutuallyExclusivePaths function and MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG constant remain exported and unchanged. Added a new test case 'throws when both project_path and cwd_path are provided' in tests/utils/path-validator.test.ts. Updated the obsolete 'prefers project_path over cwd_path when both are provided' test in tests/tools/workflow-next-action.test.ts to reflect the new error-throwing behavior. All 1014 tests pass, TypeScript compiles clean.

comments.note: The test file tests/tools/workflow-next-action.test.ts had a test 'prefers project_path over cwd_path when both are provided' that documented the old silent-preference behavior. It was updated to test the new error-throwing contract as part of this WP. Consider auditing other tool test files (pipeline.test.ts, work-package.test.ts, etc.) for similar tests that may still document the old behavior—those will become relevant when WP-002 removes the .refine() calls from those schemas.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified. TypeScript compiles clean (tsc --noEmit, exit 0). Full test suite: 1014 tests across 33 files — all pass. The new mutual exclusivity guard in resolveProjectPath() throws Error(MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG) before any other logic when both project_path and cwd_path are provided (AC1 ✅). Single-path and cwd-only paths continue working (AC2 ✅, AC3 ✅). mutuallyExclusivePaths and MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG remain exported and covered by their own dedicated describe blocks (AC4 ✅). Function signature and return type unchanged (AC5 ✅). Edge cases confirmed: empty-string project_path with a truthy cwd_path correctly bypasses the guard (falsy short-circuit) and falls through to cwd-path resolution — consistent with mutuallyExclusivePaths semantics; this is tested. Integration-level verification in workflow-next-action.test.ts confirms the MCP tool surfaces the error as isError: true with text matching the mutual exclusivity message pattern. No regressions found.

comments.note: Edge-case scrutiny: empty-string project_path ('') with a non-empty cwd_path does not trigger the mutual exclusivity guard because the check uses truthy evaluation ('' && cwd_path is falsy). This is intentional and consistent with mutuallyExclusivePaths behaviour, and is explicitly tested. No issue.

Developer's improvement note is well-founded: other tool schemas (pipeline, work-package, etc.) still have .refine(mutuallyExclusivePaths) in their Zod schemas; those become redundant dead code after this WP but cause no functional harm until WP-002 removes them. Out of scope for this WP.

summary: Code review passed. The mutual exclusivity guard is correctly placed at the top of resolveProjectPath(), fails fast before any other logic, reuses MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG for consistent messaging between runtime and Zod paths, and uses truthy evaluation that is exactly consistent with the pre-existing mutuallyExclusivePaths predicate. The inline comment referencing the bug report provides clear historical context. New unit test is well-placed and asserts using the constant directly. Integration test in workflow-next-action.test.ts correctly verifies both isError:true and message shape. The empty-string edge case is intentional, consistent with mutuallyExclusivePaths semantics, and explicitly covered.

comments.note: The integration test regex /project_path.*cwd_path|cwd_path.*project_path/i is intentionally loose for resilience, which is an acceptable pattern for MCP tool integration tests. Could equally be written against MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG directly if the constant gets imported into the test file, but the current approach is not a problem.

mutuallyExclusivePaths predicate and its Zod .refine() calls in other tool schemas are now redundant dead-code for the project_path+cwd_path conflict case. They cause no functional harm, but WP-002 cleanup is the correct venue. The exports must remain available for backward-compatible use (e.g., a caller constructing their own Zod schema), so removal should be done carefully in WP-002.
